key_insight: Burst restarts in wall turbulence can be explained without assuming streak dependence, by a forced linearized model in which vortex breakup and catch-up dynamics drive a restart process characterized by linearly available energy (LAE).
engineering_relevance: This gives a mechanistic, low-order way to predict and interpret burst reactivation in near-wall flows, which is useful for turbulence modeling and control in wall-bounded CFD.
method: Formulated forced linearized Navier–Stokes restart problems in a log-minimal channel.
Used optimization to identify minimal conditions for burst-restart-like solutions.
Interpreted restart stages through spanwise-vorticity evolution and defined LAE as a progress metric.
evidence_signal: The paper combines analytical/optimization results from the linearized model with flow-pattern extraction from real turbulence during restarting stages.
watch_item: The conclusions depend on a log-minimal channel setup and a forcing-based decomposition, so extension to full-range geometries or different Reynolds-number regimes may need validation.
paper_title: Restarts of bursts in turbulence in a log-minimal channel
